full_counterpart.description_long: Donald Trump fired sitting members of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission in January 2025, including Democratic and Republican appointees whose terms had not expired. Without enough commissioners to form a quorum, the EEOC could not take certain agency decisions, interrupting parts of its enforcement work under laws against discrimination based on race, sex, religion, national origin, age and disability. Federal courts later found the removals unlawful for commissioners protected by statutory terms. Those rulings addressed the limits Congress placed on removing protected officials, rather than every presidential removal from an independent agency. Civil-rights organizations criticized the firings as a severe attack on federal anti-discrimination enforcement. The loss of a quorum also affected the agency’s ability to resolve matters requiring commission action while the litigation proceeded. The dispute centered on whether the president could remove commissioners before their terms ended and how statutory protections preserve the EEOC’s ability to enforce workplace civil-rights laws.
full_counterpart.description_medium: In January 2025, Donald Trump removed sitting members of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, including commissioners with unexpired terms. The action left the EEOC without a decision-making quorum and interrupted its ability to enforce federal workplace anti-discrimination laws. Federal courts later found the removals unlawful where statutory term protections applied, raising questions about presidential authority and the continuity of civil-rights enforcement.
full_counterpart.description_short: Trump Fires All EEOC Commissioners — Paralyzes Anti-Discrimination Enforcement
